subject: PrivDep BYOK: operator scopes and cross-border solutioning
messages:
From: Michael Santos <michael.santos@mediex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@mediex.com
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment — BYOK expectations and operator access

Marissa — thanks for the call this morning. We have internal stakeholders who want the following clarified before we can sign the DPA addendum and move forward with the private deployment POC: 1) the exact operational activities Redwood operators are allowed to perform in a customer-controlled KMS/VPC setup; 2) whether any telemetry or logs that reference customer identifiers can leave our region; 3) an emergency "breakglass" procedure and evidence that Redwood cannot decrypt customer keys.

Attached is a sketch of our desired dataflow and a short markup of the DPA with inline questions. Can your team propose crisp contract language for operator scope and cross-border limits?

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Santos
VP Engineering, MediEx

Attachments: dataflow_diagram_v2.png, dpa_markup_20281209.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Santos <michael.santos@mediex.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment — BYOK expectations and operator access

Michael — appreciate the clear list and the diagram. I've looped in our security and legal owners to propose specific language. Quick summary of our current posture for reference: 1) Customer provides CMKs (BYOK) — Redwood does not persist plaintext key material and only receives wrapped key blobs for HSM import when required by the deployment pattern; 2) Operator activities (support, restarts, configuration) are limited to roles we enumerate in the DPA annex; 3) Telemetry we collect is telemetry-only (runtime metrics, aggregated request counts) and is scrubbed of direct customer IDs by default; 4) Breakglass requires multi-party approval and results in a timeboxed, auditable session with exportable logs.

We will produce a short redline to your DPA and a separate "operator scope" annex that lists permitted actions and evidence channels. Propose a 1-week turnaround — can you confirm the internal reviewers and any procurement timelines?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Santos <michael.santos@mediex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Dec 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment — BYOK expectations and operator access

Michael, Marissa — attaching the first draft of two items: (A) "Operator Scope Annex" (PDF) and (B) proposed DPA redline. High level notes in the cover: 1) Operator scope is principle-of-least-privilege — we enumerate role names (Platform Operator, Support Engineer, Escalation Engineer) and concrete actions (apply node OS updates, restart inference runtime, rotate service certificates) — and we explicitly exclude key material extraction and any action that would result in learning plaintext customer secrets; 2) Cross-border telemetry — by default telemetry is collected and stored in the deployment region. We propose clause: "Telemetry containing customer identifiers or payload-derived metadata shall not be transferred out of the region without Customer written consent and an amendment to the DPA"; 3) Breakglass — we propose a 3-person approval (Customer SRE, Redwood Security, Redwood CTO delegated) and a forced live recording of the session plus signed attestation; 4) Escrow/Recovery — optional but we propose an escrow process only if customer opts in; Redwood will refuse escrow by default for BYOK.

We flagged a couple of places for legal to weigh in on "forensic exports" and "consent to transfer" language. Laura, can you look at the redlines (docx) and propose the exact contract text?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: privdep_operator_scope_draft.pdf, dpa_redline_20281210.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Santos <michael.santos@mediex.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Dec 2028 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment — BYOK expectations and operator access

Michael — thanks for the patience. I reviewed the redline and made the following suggested contract language bullets (included in the attached DOCX): 
- Define "Operator Activities" as a closed list and require Customer written sign-off to expand the list; 
- Add affirmative statement: "Redwood does not and will not access plaintext customer key material under BYOK deployments without an explicit, time-limited, documented, and auditable emergency approval process"; 
- Telemetry clause: "Aggregate runtime telemetry retained for <90 days; telemetry that includes customer IDs or request payload hashes shall be stored in-region and exported only pursuant to Customer written consent"; 
- Forensic export: require a formal preservation request and a narrow scope.

Law note: we cannot sign an irrevocable refusal to escrow in the DPA; instead we offer an "escrow opt-out by default" commercial term in the SOW and will only engage escrow under a separate, negotiable schedule with additional security safeguards.

Next steps: I'm happy to iterate on the exact wording. Michael, if you can propose the exact acceptance criteria we should use for the POC (e.g., evidence artifacts, minimal telemetry fields), we'll bake that into the SOW annex and checklist.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Santos <michael.santos@mediex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Dec 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment — BYOK expectations and operator access

Team — this looks good and addresses many of our concerns. A couple quick clarifications before we route to procurement: 1) acceptance criteria for POC: must include (a) a recorded breakglass drill (tabletop + live) where Redwood demonstrates the approval flow and provides the attestation; (b) evidence bundle: audit logs for operator sessions, in-region telemetry export sample, and signed hash of key import events; 2) escrow: MediEx will initially accept the "escrow opt-out by default" model but wants an SLA that limits Redwood's ability to compel a different path without 60 days' notice and mutual agreement; 3) cross-border transfers: we want the explicit telemetry-in-region clause in the DPA body (not just annex).

I'll have procurement try to turn this around next week. Can we schedule the POC breakglass drill for week of Jan 8? Aditya — can you scope resources needed for the runbook?

Thanks,
Michael
VP Engineering, MediEx
